name: LAN8720AI-CP-TR
title: LAN8720A / LAN8720Ai: 10/100 Ethernet PHY with RMII, HP Auto-MDIX and variable-voltage I/O, 24-pin QFN 4 x 4 mm
summary: A single-port physical layer transceiver for 10BASE-T and 100BASE-TX Ethernet that talks to a MAC over the reduced pin count RMII bus and is managed over MDIO/MDC. It negotiates speed and duplex on its own, swaps its transmit and receive pairs for straight or crossed cables (HP Auto-MDIX), and needs no register writes to run: pin straps set the PHY address, the start-up mode, the internal 1.2 V regulator and the clocking mode. The analog side runs from 3.3 V, the digital I/O from 1.62 V to 3.6 V, and the 1.2 V core comes from an on-chip linear regulator or an outside supply. The RMII reference is either a 50 MHz clock fed in or a 50 MHz clock the part makes from a 25 MHz crystal. LAN8720A is the 0 to +85 °C grade, LAN8720Ai the -40 to +85 °C grade.

RMII (50 MHz REF_CLK, 2-bit data); SMI management (MDIO/MDC)

pins.name: VDD2A
pins.function: 3.3 V analog supply for channel 2; also feeds the internal 1.2 V regulator.

pins.name: LED2/nINTSEL
pins.function: LED2 (O12) goes active at 100 Mbit/s and inactive at 10 Mbit/s or while the line is isolated. Latched at reset as nINTSEL (IS, internal pull-up): high or open selects REF_CLK In mode with nINT on pin 14; low selects REF_CLK Out mode with REFCLKO on pin 14. The strap level also sets the LED polarity. A pull-up goes to VDD2A.

pins.name: LED1/REGOFF
pins.function: LED1 (O12) is on while a link is up and blinks on activity. Latched at reset as REGOFF (IS, internal pull-down): open or low keeps the internal 1.2 V regulator on; pulled up to VDD2A it turns the regulator off and VDDCR must be supplied from outside. The strap level also sets the LED polarity.

pins.name: XTAL2
pins.function: Crystal output (OCLK). Left open when a single-ended clock drives pin 5.

pins.name: XTAL1/CLKIN
pins.function: Crystal input, or single-ended clock input (ICLK): 25 MHz in REF_CLK Out mode, the 50 MHz REF_CLK in REF_CLK In mode.

pins.name: VDDCR
pins.function: 1.2 V digital core supply. Fed by the internal regulator unless REGOFF disables it. Decouple to ground with 1 µF and 470 pF in parallel.

pins.name: RXD1/MODE1
pins.function: Receive data bit 1 to the MAC (VO8). Latched at reset as MODE1 (VIS, internal pull-up), one of the three bits that pick the start-up mode.

pins.name: RXD0/MODE0
pins.function: Receive data bit 0 to the MAC (VO8). Latched at reset as MODE0 (VIS, internal pull-up).

pins.name: VDDIO
pins.function: Supply for the digital I/O, 1.62 V to 3.6 V.

pins.name: RXER/PHYAD0
pins.function: Receive error to the MAC (VO8): high when the frame being passed on holds an error. Latched at reset as PHYAD0 (VIS, internal pull-down), bit 0 of the SMI address.

pins.name: CRS_DV/MODE2
pins.function: Carrier sense and receive data valid (VO8): high while the line is not idle. On a 10BASE-T packet RXD[1:0] stays low until the SFD byte (10101011) arrives. Transmit data is not echoed onto receive in 10BASE-T half duplex. Latched at reset as MODE2 (VIS, internal pull-up).

pins.name: MDIO
pins.function: SMI management data in and out (VIS input, VOD8 open-drain output).

pins.name: MDC
pins.function: SMI management clock (VIS).

pins.name: nINT/REFCLKO
pins.function: With nINTSEL high: nINT, active-low open-drain interrupt (VOD8, internal pull-up); fit an outside pull-up to VDDIO. With nINTSEL low: REFCLKO, a 50 MHz RMII clock (VO8) made from the 25 MHz crystal or oscillator.

pins.name: nRST
pins.function: Active-low hardware reset (VIS, internal pull-up). A reset is required after power-up.

pins.name: TXEN
pins.function: Transmit enable from the MAC (VIS, internal pull-down): high while TXD[1:0] carries valid data.

pins.name: TXD0
pins.function: Transmit data bit 0 from the MAC (VIS).

pins.name: TXD1
pins.function: Transmit data bit 1 from the MAC (VIS).

pins.name: VDD1A
pins.function: 3.3 V analog supply for channel 1.

pins.name: TXN
pins.function: Channel 1 negative line (AIO): transmit pair in MDI, receive pair when Auto-MDIX swaps.

pins.name: TXP
pins.function: Channel 1 positive line (AIO).

pins.name: RXN
pins.function: Channel 2 negative line (AIO): receive pair in MDI, transmit pair when swapped.

pins.name: RXP
pins.function: Channel 2 positive line (AIO).

pins.name: RBIAS
pins.function: Bias set point: a 12.1 kΩ 1 % resistor to ground. Nominal pin voltage 1.2 V; the resistor dissipates about 1 mW.

pins.name: VSS
pins.function: Exposed pad, ground. Connect it to the ground plane through an array of vias.

operation.text: One 10/100 Ethernet port between an RMII MAC and the line magnetics. It carries IEEE 802.3-2005 compliant registers plus vendor registers, yet none has to be written: the straps choose the start-up setup and registers refine it. Its digital pins tolerate 3.6 V. A single 3.3 V supply is enough when the internal 3.3 V to 1.2 V linear regulator is used; that regulator can be turned off so an efficient outside regulator powers the core instead.

Two transmit bits (TXD[1:0]) with TXEN, two receive bits (RXD[1:0]) with CRS_DV and an optional RXER, all timed by one 50 MHz REF_CLK, at 10 or 100 Mbit/s, with LVCMOS levels. MDIO/MDC management is the same as on MII. The transmit path uses REF_CLK directly with no buffering; the receive path recovers the line clock and an elasticity buffer absorbs the difference to REF_CLK. The PHY latches TXD on the rising REF_CLK edge and launches RXD on the falling edge so the MAC can sample on the rising one. TXD[1:0] must be 00 while TXEN is low; other values are reserved and ignored.

CRS_DV rises asynchronously as soon as carrier is found: squelch passed in 10BASE-T, or two non-adjacent zeros within 10 bits in 100BASE-X. RXD[1:0] reads 00 until decoding is valid. When carrier ends while bits are still queued, CRS_DV toggles on nibble boundaries, 25 MHz at 100 Mbit/s and 2.5 MHz at 10 Mbit/s, so the MAC can separate carrier from data valid. On a false carrier it stays high for as long as the activity lasts. In full duplex or repeater mode carrier sense follows receive activity only; otherwise it follows transmit or receive.
With nINTSEL high or open, an outside 50 MHz source drives XTAL1/CLKIN and the MAC together, XTAL2 is left open, and pin 14 is the nINT interrupt. This is the standard RMII arrangement.

With nINTSEL pulled low the part builds the 50 MHz REF_CLK from a 25 MHz fundamental crystal (cheaper than a 50 MHz third-overtone crystal) or from a 25 MHz clock on XTAL1/CLKIN, and sends it to the MAC on REFCLKO. The input must then be 25 MHz, not 50 MHz. The interrupt output is lost because REFCLKO shares its pin. The MAC has to accept an outside REF_CLK. This mode lies outside the RMII specification and its timing does not comply with it, so the MAC-to-PHY timing has to be analysed for each design.

PHYAD0, MODE[2:0], REGOFF and nINTSEL share pins with outputs and are latched at power-on reset and on nRST. Each has an internal pull so it reads a defined level when open; where the pin also drives a load, an outside resistor must back up or override the internal one so the level is right before latching, within the tcss/tcsh times. Pull-ups go to VDDIO, except REGOFF and nINTSEL, which go to VDD2A (as do LED pull-ups). A soft reset leaves the straps unused and keeps the register values.

PHYAD0 (on RXER) sets the SMI address to 0 or 1 when a hardware reset finishes; it defaults to 0. Higher addresses are written into the PHYAD bits of register 18 once the PHY answers at its strapped address. The address also seeds the scrambler, so several PHYs on one board scramble differently and spread their emissions.
MODE[2:0] loads the speed, duplex and auto-negotiation bits of registers 0 and 4 when nRST is released; the register values then govern. Software may rewrite those registers at any time.

With REGOFF open or low (internal pull-down) the regulator starts from VDD2A once it samples REGOFF below VIL, and nothing has to feed VDDCR. With a pull-up from REGOFF to VDD2A the part samples it above VIH after VDDIO and VDD2A are in range, keeps the regulator off, and VDDCR must come from outside. In that case VDDIO has to reach 80 % of its level before VDDCR is applied: 1.44 V for 1.8 V, 2.0 V for 2.5 V, 2.64 V for 3.3 V. An outside switching regulator lowers system power against the internal linear one.

LED1 lights on a valid link and blinks while CRS is active; LED2 lights at 100 Mbit/s and goes dark at 10 Mbit/s or during isolation. Each LED output takes the polarity opposite to its strap: an outside pull-up to VDD2A on LED1/REGOFF (regulator off) makes LED1 active low, the internal pull-down makes it active high; LED2/nINTSEL left high (nINT mode) is active low, and an outside pull-down (REFCLKO mode) makes it active high. LED pull-ups must go to VDD2A, never VDDIO. Typical values are about 270 Ω in series with the LED and 10 kΩ for a strap resistor.

The digital pins run from a VDDIO of 1.62 V to 3.6 V. VDDIO must hold within ±10 %, and changing it once power-on reset is over may upset operation. No input may be pulled high while the part is still unpowered.

The 3.3 V supplies, VDDIO and the magnetics supply may come up in any order within 50 ms and go down in any order within 500 ms. A hardware reset is required after power-up: nRST may be asserted any time but must stay low at least 100 µs and not be released until 25 ms after all supplies pass 80 %. The clock on XTAL1/CLKIN must be running during a hardware reset. Outputs float within 50 ns of nRST going low and drive again 2 ns to 800 ns after it rises.

Setting bit 0.15 resets every register bit except those marked NASR; the bit clears itself and the reset finishes within 0.5 s, as IEEE 802.3u clause 22 requires. The power-down modes do not reset registers. For the first 16 µs after any reset the RMII runs at 2.5 MHz, then moves to 25 MHz if auto-negotiation is on.

General power-down (bit 0.11) stops everything except the management interface until the bit is cleared, after which the PHY powers up and resets itself. Energy detect power-down (bit 17.13) keeps only management, squelch and the ENERGYON logic alive while the line is quiet; when link pulses or packets arrive ENERGYON goes high, the PHY wakes into its previous state and can raise nINT. The first one or two packets may be lost on wake-up.
Bit 0.10 disconnects the data path from the RMII: TXD, TXEN and TXER are ignored but management still works, so several PHYs can share one RMII bus. The part starts not isolated.

IEEE 802.3 clause 28 negotiation with Fast Link Pulse bursts of up to 33 pulses (17 clock, 16 data). It starts on hardware, software or power-down reset, on link loss, or on setting bit 0.9. Priority order: 100 full, 100 half, 10 full, 10 half. Advertised abilities come from the MODE straps and can be changed in register 4 bits 8 to 5, which take effect only after a restart. A restart from software drops the link for the break_link_timer, about 1200 ms. Next Page is not supported. With auto-negotiation off, bits 0.13 and 0.8 force speed and duplex.

Against a partner that does not negotiate, the PHY picks the speed from MLT-3 symbols or 10 Mbit/s link pulses and assumes half duplex; bit 6.0 then reads 0 and register 5 shows the partner's speed. A fault in this process sets bit 6.4.

The PHY senses which pair the partner transmits on and swaps TXP/TXN with RXP/RXN, so straight and crossover cables both work, on CAT-3 for 10BASE-T or CAT-5 for 100BASE-TX. Because the pairs swap, the magnetics and termination of both pairs have to be laid out alike. Bit 27.15 turns the feature off, and 27.13 then picks MDI or MDIX by hand.

Dibits from the RMII are gathered into nibbles, coded 4B/5B, scrambled (seeded from PHYAD) and serialised, turned into a 125 MHz NRZI stream and then into three-level MLT-3, which the driver puts on TXP/TXN through a 1:1 transformer into the 100 Ω cable. The 10 and 100 Mbit/s signals share the same magnetics. Termination and impedance matching are outside parts. A PLL locked to the reference makes the 125 MHz clock.

Signal from a 1:1 transformer is sampled at 125 Msample/s by a 6-bit (64-level) ADC whose gain the DSP adjusts. The equalizer handles good CAT-5 from 1 m to 150 m, baseline wander is corrected (the FDDI TP-PMD killer packet is received without errors) and a multi-phase 125 MHz clock picks the best sampling point. The descrambler locks on IDLE symbols and must see IDLE within a 4000-byte (40 µs) window, which allows a 1514-byte frame; otherwise it resynchronises. /J/K/ starts a frame and becomes 0101 0101 of the preamble; /T/R/ or two IDLEs end it. A bad code group inside a frame raises RXER with arbitrary data; a bad start delimiter raises RXER with 1110 on the data lines.

Nibbles are Manchester coded with a 20 MHz clock from the 10M PLL and sent through the magnetics; with no data, normal link pulses keep the link. In half duplex the transmitted data is looped onto the receive path for older MACs, and SQE (heartbeat) is supported. The receiver filters, then a squelch rejects differential signals below 300 mV and accepts them above 585 mV. Reversed polarity on the pair is found and corrected and shown in bit 27.4. Jabber (TXEN held too long) stops transmission within 45 ms and resets when TXEN falls; bit 1.1 reports it.

Link status follows the IEEE 802.3u link monitor and drives bit 1.2 and LED1. Once the DSP reports a valid MLT-3 signal the logic waits at least 330 µs before Link-Ready, then goes Link-Up when auto-negotiation allows (at once if it is off). Losing the signal drops the link at once. In 10BASE-T the link comes from the 10BASE-T receiver.

Near-end loopback (bit 0.14) sends transmit data back to the receive pins through the PCS and PMA into the PMD, with the line drivers off whatever TXEN does. Far loopback (bit 17.9) returns what the link partner sends back to it over the MDI while the MAC side is isolated. Connector loopback works at 10 and 100 Mbit/s with an RJ45 plug that ties pin 1 to 3 and pin 2 to 6.

Registers 0 to 6 (IEEE clause 22) and vendor registers 16 to 31 are reachable; others read FFFFh. MDC comes from the management controller and has no upper limit on period; edges must be at least 160 ns apart and a full cycle at least 400 ns, slow enough for a microcontroller port. MDIO is sampled on the rising MDC edge. A frame is 32 ones of preamble, start 01, opcode 10 for read or 01 for write, a 5-bit PHY address, a 5-bit register address, a turnaround and 16 data bits, most significant first.

nINT (open drain, active low, needs a pull-up to VDDIO) asserts for each source enabled in register 30. In the default primary mode it releases when the source condition ends or the flag register 29 is read. In the alternate mode (bit 17.6) it releases only when the mask bit is cleared, or when the source has ended and a 1 is written to the flag bit. The interrupt is not available in REF_CLK Out mode.
RBIAS takes a 12.1 kΩ 1 % resistor to ground. VDDCR takes 1 µF and 470 pF in parallel to ground. The exposed pad is the ground and needs a via array into the ground plane.

Each of TXP, TXN, RXP, RXN has a 49.9 Ω resistor to the supply that also feeds the chip-side centre taps of the magnetics, which are bypassed to ground. On the cable side each centre tap goes through 75 Ω to a common node returned to chassis ground by 1000 pF rated 3 kV. With one 3.3 V supply the termination rail is the 3.3 V rail through a ferrite bead, and VDD1A and VDD2A are taken after the bead. With two supplies the analog pins stay on 3.3 V while the terminations and centre taps run from a separate 2.5 V to 3.3 V rail.

circuits.title: Power supply, 1.2 V from the internal regulator
circuits.description: Supply hookup with the core regulator running. One 3.3 V supply feeds both analog pins, each with its own bypass capacitor; VDD2A also powers the regulator, whose output on VDDCR is decoupled by 1 µF and 470 pF. A separate 1.8 V to 3.3 V rail feeds VDDIO with CF and a bypass capacitor. RBIAS has its 12.1 kΩ to ground. LED1/REGOFF drives an LED to ground through about 270 Ω; with REGOFF low the regulator is on and LED1 is active high.

circuits.title: Power supply, 1.2 V from an outside source
circuits.description: Supply hookup with the core regulator turned off. A 10 kΩ pull-up from LED1/REGOFF to the 3.3 V rail straps REGOFF high, so an outside 1.2 V supply feeds VDDCR, decoupled by 1 µF and 470 pF. The LED now runs from 3.3 V through about 270 Ω into LED1, which is active low. The analog pins, VDDIO and RBIAS are wired as with the internal regulator.

circuits.title: Twisted-pair interface, single supply
circuits.description: Line side from one 3.3 V supply. The supply passes a ferrite bead; after the bead it feeds VDD1A and VDD2A (each bypassed), four 49.9 Ω resistors, one from each of TXP, TXN, RXP and RXN, and the chip-side centre taps of both transformers, bypassed to ground. On the cable side the transformers go to RJ45 pins 1-2 and 3-6; each cable-side centre tap passes through 75 Ω to a node that 1000 pF, 3 kV returns to chassis ground. RJ45 pins 4, 5, 7 and 8 are left unconnected.

1:1 with centre taps; pins P1, PCT, P2 chip side, S1, SCT, S2 cable side

circuits.title: Twisted-pair interface, dual supplies
circuits.description: Line side with two supplies. VDD1A and VDD2A run from 3.3 V with a bypass capacitor each. A second rail of 2.5 V to 3.3 V feeds four 49.9 Ω resistors, one from each of TXP, TXN, RXP and RXN, and the chip-side centre taps of both transformers, bypassed to ground. On the cable side the transformers go to RJ45 pins 1-2 and 3-6; each cable-side centre tap passes through 75 Ω to a node that 1000 pF, 3 kV returns to chassis ground. RJ45 pins 4, 5, 7 and 8 are left unconnected.

1:1 with centre taps; pins P1, PCT, P2 chip side, S1, SCT, S2 cable side

circuits.title: LED1 with REGOFF strapped high (regulator off)
circuits.description: A 10 kΩ from VDD2A pulls LED1/REGOFF high, turning the internal regulator off. The LED runs from VDD2A through about 270 Ω into the pin, which then drives active low.

circuits.title: LED1 with REGOFF low (regulator on)
circuits.description: The internal pull-down holds LED1/REGOFF low, so the regulator stays on. The pin drives the LED active high to ground through about 270 Ω.

circuits.title: LED2 with nINTSEL high (nINT mode)
circuits.description: The internal pull-up on LED2/nINTSEL leaves the strap high, keeping pin 14 as nINT. The LED runs from VDD2A through about 270 Ω into the pin, which drives active low.

circuits.title: LED2 with nINTSEL low (REFCLKO mode)
circuits.description: A 10 kΩ from LED2/nINTSEL to ground straps nINTSEL low, selecting REFCLKO on pin 14. The pin drives the LED active high to ground through about 270 Ω.

circuits.title: REF_CLK In mode: outside 50 MHz clock
circuits.description: System hookup in REF_CLK In mode. A 50 MHz reference drives the MAC's REF_CLK and the PHY's XTAL1/CLKIN together, and every RMII signal is timed by it; XTAL2 stays open. The RMII lines, MDIO, MDC and nINT run straight between MAC and PHY; the four line pins go to the magnetics and RJ45, and LED1, LED2 and nRST go to the rest of the system.

circuits.title: REF_CLK Out mode: 25 MHz crystal
circuits.description: System hookup in REF_CLK Out mode. A 25 MHz crystal sits across XTAL1/CLKIN and XTAL2, and the PHY sends the 50 MHz REF_CLK it derives from REFCLKO to the MAC, which must accept an outside 50 MHz clock. nINT is not available. The other RMII and management lines, the line pins, LEDs and nRST are wired as in REF_CLK In mode.
notes: The crystal table gives the XTAL1/CLKIN and XTAL2 pin capacitances used to size the two load capacitors.

circuits.title: REF_CLK Out mode: outside 25 MHz clock
circuits.description: System hookup in REF_CLK Out mode from a 25 MHz clock already on the board. The clock drives XTAL1/CLKIN, XTAL2 stays open, and REFCLKO gives the MAC its 50 MHz REF_CLK. The input has to be 25 MHz; a 50 MHz clock does not work in this hookup. nINT is not available.
